summary: Mid-window synchronized warmup waves causing reserved pool thinness and transient throughput collapse
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart reported a sharp mid-day throughput collapse (p50 and p95 token throughput drops) in their dedicated reserved pool. The drop coincided with increased 502/5xx from generation endpoints and a rise in request queuing. Initial symptoms indicate transient GPU attach failures and queuing; not a long-lived hardware failure.

Narrative: At ~11:30 US‑East BrightCart observed a sustained ~60% throughput reduction for their most used generation route for ~12 minutes, with a small spike in 5xx and repeated internal timeouts. The pool autoscaler did not create new capacity during the window and a number of tenant-side background jobs (warmup + validation) were observed running simultaneously across co-located tenants. This ticket tracks investigation and mitigation for coordinated warmup waves and noisy-neighbor interactions causing reserved-pool thinness.
impact: Customer-facing generation latency increased (p50 throughput down ~60%, p95 increased from 1.2s to 4.6s). Several 1-minute spikes of 502 returned to caller. Multiple BrightCart routes affected for the 12-minute window during business hours. Revenue-impacting for the customer; they are on committed reserved capacity and expect predictable throughput.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated reserved pool in us-east, schedule model warmup cron at 11:30 for multiple tenants simultaneously.
2) Trigger a normal traffic pattern for BrightCart generation route with typical fanout (5-10 concurrent streams).
3) Observe autoscaler and allocator behavior; verify GPU attach success and queue length metrics.
4) Re-run with background validation sweep enabled on a second tenant to reproduce interaction effects.
observed_behavior: Synchronized warmup+validation tasks from multiple tenants caused short-lived high demand on prefetch/KV operations and GPU attach. GPU attach latencies spiked, allocator credit fell, and the autoscaler metric stream (smoothed attach failures + attach latency) did not cross the scale-up threshold quickly enough. Result: transient shortage of attach-ready GPU slots and request queuing.
expected_behavior: Dedicated reserved pool should absorb warmup workloads without impacting production route throughput by prioritizing real-time inference requests, or autoscaler should scale fast enough to compensate for short waves of warmup load.
investigation_notes: 11:40 - SRE reproduced attach latency spike in staging by aligning two warmup cron jobs; reproduction matched production profile (attach latencies 3.5-5s).
11:55 - Observed that a background validation job introduced NVMe IO bursts on nodes servicing the reserved pool; this amplified attach latency variability.
12:10 - Autoscaler logs show smoothing window prevented immediate scale-up; bridging delay ~45s between attach latency spike and any scaling decision.

12:30 - Hypothesis: time-aligned warmup/validation waves from >1 tenant create short but sharp prefetch and NVMe IO pressure which causes transient GPU attach delays and allocator credit drain. Autoscaler thresholds tuned for longer trends missed the short pulse.
root_cause: Coordinated warmup/validation jobs across co-located tenants produced a short-duration spike in prefetch and NVMe IO, causing GPU attach latency to increase and allocator credits to be consumed. The autoscaler smoothing window and scale thresholds are tuned for sustained pressure and did not react quickly enough to a narrow high-amplitude pulse. Result: transient reserved-pool thinness and observable throughput collapse for BrightCart routes.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-10 12:05: temporarily rate-limited background validation jobs for non-critical tenants in the affected reserved pool and implemented a short-term autoscaler override to allow one fast-scale-up during detected attach-latency pulses. Customer workaround: BrightCart routed high-priority production traffic to pinned low-latency slice while mitigation in place. Full code change tracked in PR.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:12 - Luis Ortega (SRE): Applied temporary autoscaler override and throttled background validation cohorts. Observed throughput recovering at 12:17.
2026-03-10 15:04 - Maya Patel (Support): Customer confirmed service restored and accepted the pinned-slice workaround for the rest of the day.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Elena Ruiz (Platform Eng): Kernel-level NVMe IO diagnostics show correlation between snapshotter writes and attach latency; scheduled deeper analysis.
2026-03-13 10:22 - Luis Ortega (SRE): PR for autoscaler pulse-detection submitted; awaiting review. Temporary mitigations remain in place for the pool.
next_steps: 1) Merge autoscaler pulse-detection PR and deploy canary to us-east reserved pools. 2) Add soft coordination to warmup cron schedules to avoid strict alignment across tenants in same pool. 3) Create a pool-level policy to deprioritize warmup/validation prefetch during business hours for enterprise tenants. 4) Postmortem and best-practice doc for customers.
notes_for_postmortem: Avoid owner-blaming; focus on system-level coupling between scheduled background work and autoscaler design. Capture timeline, graphs, and the pulse-detection tuning rationale.
customer_comms: We informed BrightCart of root-cause hypothesis, the immediate mitigations we applied (throttling background validation tasks + temporary autoscaler override), and the roadmap for a permanent fix. BrightCart requested a post-incident review meeting on 2026-03-16.
resolution_status: Partial mitigation in place; awaiting autoscaler code merge for full mitigation.
